Where in installation.load_installation's first-failure order is configuration depth checked, and which module performs the non-recursive pre-parse measurement?

quotes: read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not an absolute path; it cannot be opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, each component with os.O_NOFOLLOW, whose presence is never tested, each directory on the way also with os.O_PATH and os.O_DIRECTORY and the file itself also with os.O_NONBLOCK (A17), the file so opened is not a regular file, is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read, nest deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant — depth as canonical_bytes defines it, measured on the bytes without recursion before they are parsed —, or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name. Request bounds, each counted as UTF-8 bytes of the field as received: implementation code within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_IMPLEMENTATION_CODE_BYTES_MAX constant; the json_text of a trial case input or expected output, of a flow constant and of a run input within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant; the decoded bytes of a trial case file within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant; every other string anywhere in the request within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant; a page_size given below 1 or above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_PAGE_SIZE_MAX constant; base64 text that does not decode; each a failure answered invalid_request (A16 rules 4 and 6).

answer_request: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] As part of the fit check, before the actor check and before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1).

read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not an absolute path; it cannot be opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, each component with os.O_NOFOLLOW, whose presence is never tested, each directory on the way also with os.O_PATH and os.O_DIRECTORY and the file itself also with os.O_NONBLOCK (A17), the file so opened is not a regular file, is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read, nest deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant — depth as canonical_bytes defines it, measured on the bytes without recursion before they are parsed —, or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name. The ownership, mode and regular-file checks and the read MUST all use that one opened file, so the file checked is the file read.

read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON — a record nesting deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, depth as canonical_bytes defines it, measured without recursion before it is parsed, is not valid JSON —, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

send_prepared_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] A 2xx answer with value output ports must be UTF-8 text parsing as one JSON object without duplicate member names, whatever its Content-Type, whose depth, as canonical_bytes defines depth, measured on the body as a whole without recursion before it is parsed, is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant; each output port takes the member of the same name, which must exist and fit the port by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant as size bound, so that a value's own size is judged only by the value_too_large check below, members no port names are ignored, and any failure is contract_violation; after everything else fits, a value whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant is contract_violation with detail value_too_large.

assemble_mapped_lists: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST measure every value list against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant before it answers anything, and when the canonical bytes of any exceed it, or canonical_bytes refuses the list with NonCanonicalValueError — which for a list of stored canonical values happens only when it nests deeper than the release depth ceiling —, answer ListsOverCeiling naming the node and the first such port in the order given, with no list; it is given only the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output, so every delivered list of a node is measured before any of them is written or delivered.
judgement.why: The later contracts assign embedded request JSON to surface plus canonical_values.canonical_bytes and separately assign raw pre-parse depth checks at each other ingress to its owning module.

topics.topic: State 4 request-entry validation sequence and placement of depth and carried-JSON failures
questions: Must every State 4 request flow perform the raw-message depth check after token validation and before operation/schema validation, despite State 4's stated four-step order?
What exact request-entry sequence must every State 4 flow use, and where are whole-message depth and carried-JSON canonicalization/depth failures shown?

quotes:
Every flow enters through `module:surface`, which handles one request at a time
to its end (A18 rule 3) and applies A16 rule 1 in its order — size, token,
operation schema, actor — before any operation's own check.

the request message
   nests no deeper than `json_depth_max`, measured before the message is
   parsed (A20 rule 1; the token travels in a header, so nothing before this
   walks the message), else `invalid_request`; it names a known
   operation and fits that operation's schema (rule 4), every JSON text it
   carries as a string one JCS can represent and within `json_depth_max` (A01
   rule 1, A20 rule 1) — the kernel then keeps its canonical form, the text
   itself need not be canonical —, else `invalid_request`; its actor may call that
   operation at all (rule 3);
judgement.divergence: State 4 directs surface to proceed size → token → operation/schema → actor, while amended A16 requires size → token → whole-message depth → operation/schema plus carried-JSON canonicalization/depth → actor; a request failing both depth and schema or authorization receives a different first failure depending on which passage is followed.
judgement.why: The State 4 entry sequence omits checks that amended A16 explicitly inserts before schema validation and actor authorization.
